title: OpenPose Wrist Heatmap
subtitle: Where the wrists went, piled into one picture
description: Runs the body OpenPose model over a video and piles up where the wrists went into a heatmap. The repo name says hands; the model only ever knew about wrists.
longDescription: A file-based demo that samples every 30th frame of a video, runs the six-stage body OpenPose network (19 heatmap and 38 part-affinity channels) at two scales, takes the lowest point of each arm/wrist region, keeps the points that fall inside configured polygon ROIs, and accumulates them into heatmap overlays saved as PNG files. It does not infer finger landmarks or hand articulation. The demo runs with Docker Compose on a CPU image with Python 3.12, TensorFlow 2.21 and tf-keras, loading the original Keras weights; the heatmap rendering derives from HeatMappy and the pose code from Open-Pose-Keras.
features: Samples every 30th frame and runs pose inference at two scales
Wrist-region points from body pose (no finger landmarks)
Polygon ROIs combined as a union mask
Accumulated motion heatmaps saved as PNG overlays
Clear errors for missing, unreadable or empty videos
One-command run with docker compose up
challenges: Keeping the original Keras model and HDF5 weights loading on current TensorFlow
Overlapping ROI masks wrapping 8-bit pixel values and darkening the image
Being honest about what the model detects: wrists, not hands
solutions: Used tf-keras 2.21 with public Keras 2 layer imports, preserving the original architecture and weight loader
Combined ROI masks as a union and rebuilt them whenever the frame size changes
Documented the body model's 19 heatmap and 38 part-affinity channels in the README and on the cover
results: Motion heatmaps for a whole video from a single Docker command
A reproducible CPU image on Python 3.12 and TensorFlow 2.21
